prerequisites: Successful completion of the StEOP (Study Induction and Orientation Phase)

learning_outcomes.text: Summarize the historical development of surface technology.
Concisely describe the principles of tribology and wear.
Present fundamental concepts of surface technology.
Perform application-oriented methods of surface modification.
Fundamentally classify the most important materials for surface coating, especially for metallic materials.
Independently perform basic methods for synthesis and characterization in the field of surface technology.
Critically discuss case studies in plenary, partner, and group work.
Concisely summarize key statements from discussions.
Apply what has been learned in practical laboratory exercises.
Conduct experimental procedures in the laboratory in a structured and safe manner.
Critically evaluate the results of practical application and observations.
Independently perform presented methods under supervision in the laboratory.
Write comprehensible and independent laboratory protocols and evaluations.

syllabus_topics: Brief overview of surface technology and its historical development
Contact of solid surfaces, principles of tribology and wear
Surface modification by mechanical, thermal, and thermo-chemical processes
Mechanical, thermal, thermo-mechanical, chemical, and electrochemical processes
Physical Vapor Deposition (PVD) and Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD)
Overview of the essential principles in PVD-based deposition methods and the most important characterization techniques
Methods for mechanical characterization of thin films
Methods for thermal characterization of thin films
Methods for chemical and structural analysis
teaching_methods: Students independently perform and learn methods in the lab under supervision

assessment_methods.method: Written and/or oral exam (for the lecture part)
Laboratory protocol / presentation of performed methods (for the laboratory exercise part)

assessment_rules: The assessment for the lecture part (VO) is a written and/or oral exam. The performance record for the laboratory exercise part (LU) is provided in the form of a protocol or a presentation of the methods performed. Specific grading formulas or resit arrangements are not detailed in the syllabus.
